policy: Every integrated interactive GUI and panel must be captured at each supported test resolution and reviewed. Third-party candidates are not assumed covered until installed and automated.

integrated_surfaces.description: Contract tab, in native Minecraft Screen
Skills tab: three columns (legal, trade with the foundation, utility and crossover skills, underground), up to six rows that scroll, selected node detail with its effect line and the unlock button
Regional import tab
Market tab: local law for controlled goods, buyers and trust, heat (replaces the black-market placeholder)
Guide page: first-half-hour journey checklist with the current step, a hint and a shortcut to the right page
Accepted order with enough goods
Accepted order with missing goods
Order above player career level
Player without citizenship
Provider unavailable
Regional exchange with three Ironhaven lines, one sold out
Regional exchange with insufficient credits for some purchases
Provisions desk of a wayside shelter: a few basics with small shared stock, no orders, location shown as Wayside desk
Imports tab outside every city exchange
Accepted recurring order consuming a crafted regional product
Recurring order locked until a rival-city exchange has been used
Public Ledger: legal postings of every trade in the city, filtered by trade, with level, reward and demand left

Notice plates stacked beside the terminal (drawn by hand for review, the game draws them in the screen corner): order accepted, delivered, contraband seized and a rare find, each with its icon, accent and words

The ninth pass's notice plates (D-187, D-189): the welcome in the chosen city, the police searching a scene and a building, and the police standing down after a logout, with the texts the server sends
The tenth pass's notice plates (D-200 to D-204): a general skill's level reached, a short shelf a career can fill, and a city's good name reached, with the texts the server sends
The civilian counter: goods for sale (rows with the same layout as the Trade page), two sections on the rail, the wallet and a daily-limit text

Status display settings with the real stack drawn at the top right below the status-effect row: place and clock, wallet and Crew bank, home and next rent, trade progress, heat, the accepted order and the next step
The same stack anchored to the left side at 120 percent, clear of the top-left corner Xaero's minimap uses and of the bottom-left chat
The stack reduced to location and wallet at 80 percent and 60 percent solidity, with the order and next-step cards switched off
Registrar conversation for a citizen already on the rolls
The counter with a wallet too small for most goods: the status 'Need N more' replaces the limit text and the buy buttons are disabled
A long list (18 goods, very long names, prices up to four digits) scrolled: nothing overlaps, the name is cut with an ellipsis, the scroll bar shows the position
The deliveries section: goods the shop buys from the citizen, with 'paid' prices and what the player is missing
An empty counter: one plain sentence, no broken rows
Entries on their last units of a daily limit: 'N left today', and a lot button that never asks for more than is left
Employer conversation: paper panel, spoken line, choice buttons (the portrait needs a world and is checked in the scripted-player run)
Guard conversation: local law and heat as spoken dialogue
Installed Q Shop marketplace with funded snapshot
Installed Q Shop marketplace with zero credits
Installed Q Shop actual trade modal opened by mouse event

Skills page, General tab (D-174, D-200): Trading, Social, Fitness, Driving and Shooting as cards with level, XP to the next level, what they give now and next and how they are earned; the Thief track in one line
Skill node that can be unlocked now (enabled UNLOCK button)
Underground node locked by points, with the reason shown
Legal licence node locked by career level, showing the prerequisite
Accepted underground contract, goods ready, buyer in another city (delivery disabled with reason)
Underground contract locked by a missing skill
Legal contract with an extra reward item and a skill requirement
Blackwater law: controlled crops permitted for a licensed grower, buyers with trust
Market tab outside every city
Secured terminal trace: the sequence being flashed
Secured terminal trace: repeating the sequence, mid-way
Secured terminal trace: last entry with the timer nearly spent
Skills tab for a level-11 Vintner (Home Distilling learned, Bootleg Trade selected) built from the real skill tree
Skills tab for a level-11 Smith built from the real skill tree
Skills tab for a level-11 Gunsmith built from the real skill tree
Skills tab for a level-11 Technician built from the real skill tree
Skills tab for a level-14 Farmer built from the real 14-skill tree, scrolled to its deepest row (Back-Lot Network selected): the scroll bar and the hint that more is above
First-login registration, step 1: choose a home city
First-login registration, step 2: choose a profession (city chosen)
First-login registration, step 3: confirm the choice and the welcome pack
Crew screen for a citizen without a Crew: found one by name
Crew screen for a citizen with two invitations to answer
Crew screen before registration: asks to register first
Crew screen when the ledger cannot be read: names the problem and the fix
Members page for a founder: roles, a selected manager, invitable players, an open invitation
Members page for a plain member: no invite or role controls, Leave Crew
Money page: Crew bank and wallet cards, quick amounts, Deposit and Withdraw, history
Money page with a payout owed, a refused request in the footer and the shared-finances proposal awaiting consent
Money page with fully shared finances in force, for a member who may spend Crew money: the bank pays first, a purchase in the history, Q Shop's own shops never use the bank
The same Crew for a member who may not spend Crew money: the bank is closed to them and they pay for purchases themselves

Home page, Your homes tab: a rented flat in good standing (hours until the next payment, hours paid ahead, deposit, storage, facilities, residents), Pay 1 h / Pay 3 h, automatic payment, Move out and the private-container controls
Home page after three unpaid hours: final-notice standing, what is owed, the footer saying nothing is lost, payment still possible
Home page for a house the Crew owns: residents, containers against the cap, the sell-back figure and the three upgrades with their prices, one fitted
Home page, Find a home tab: a motel room with the city's welcome, a flat and a house to rent or buy, with the Ironhaven price factor, For me / For the Crew and Pay from toggles

Find a home for a new player with no Crew, four credits and seven homes in reach: the free welcome rooms listed first (D-136), the page count and arrows in the tab row, clear of the first card's Rent and Buy
Home page for a player with no Crew: a rented motel room, and homes to rent or buy; the page works for everybody
Rules page, permissions tab: what Manager and Member may do
Rules page, money mode tab: three modes, shared finances waiting for consent
Rules page, money mode tab with fully shared finances in force and the limit stated: Q Shop's own shop screens never use the bank
Rules page, Crew tab: rename and the typed-name disband confirmation

Trade tab with twenty-four lines of goods (short and very long names, prices from 3 to 9,800, every stock state) and a balance that buys only some of them: nothing overlaps or runs off, the scroll bar shows
Trade tab scrolled to the end of a long list with a large balance
Trade tab where every line is sold out: the status text replaces the stock bar and the buttons are off
Lockpicking screen at the start: three pins unset, the pick far from anything, time and strain meters
Lockpicking screen with one pin set and the pick close to the next sweet spot (words and brightness, not colour alone)
Lockpicking screen pressing on the sweet spot of a four-pin lock: the pick is down, 'It gives'
Lockpicking screen pressing far off the spot with the pick strained to 88 percent and the warning lit
Lockpicking screen after the lock opened
Lockpicking screen after the pick snapped
Lockpicking screen after time ran out (nothing lost)
Alarm panel trace (D-128) while the signal shows: six symbols of a high-security panel, the 'Bypass' chip, the panel-specific help line
Alarm panel trace in the input phase, three answers in, the panel's reset timer
A fence's screen (D-125): stolen goods in the pockets by item and city of origin, the price each, sell and sell-all, the rate and the budget
The same fence with a budget too small for everything: what a sale would be cut to
A fence when the pockets hold nothing marked: the empty state and why
A shopkeeper's counter (D-126): the Trade page opened over the counter, headed with the shop's name, the city's hardware lines with stock, a sold-out line
The same counter with six credits: every purchase refused with its reason
Thief page (D-143): the Thief tree every career can follow, in three columns (locks, stealth, fencing), its own points, level and XP
Thief page of an experienced thief: most of the tree learned, the last skill selected
Thief page of a character who has never stolen anything: no points, the first skill locked by level
Casing card (D-144) for a beginner: the tier and the lock only, the rest named by the skill that would read it
Casing card for a thief with Casing and Routines: alarm, cameras, who is in, when it is empty, the safe, a recent break-in
Casing card at a door the thief cannot try: a high-security lock without a Pro Pick Set
Personal computer (D-158), the Service app: the city's service calls and jobs, the pay, how long open, whether this player may take it, Track
Personal computer, the Designs app: what an Electronics Bench makes, the parts carried against the parts needed, designs that need a skill
Electronics Bench (D-158): designs ready, missing parts or needing a skill; the selected design's parts and Assemble
A repair at a utility panel (D-158): the circuit in two branches, two test points read, the scanner's outlined stretch, Probe and Replace
An install at a utility panel (D-158): the patch grid of cable tiles, the feed, three devices to feed
Lock screen with a spool pin announced (Feel for the Pins, D-145)
Lock screen the moment a spool pin turned back
Lock screen with the Rake button (Raking, D-143)

Personal computer (D-166), the Service app with a back-channel job selected: shown only to a Technician with Bypass Tooling, in the underground colour, what it does and its risk, asking for a Bypass Kit
Back-channel work at a utility panel (D-166): the same abstract patch grid as an install, titled and coloured as underground work
A workshop station (D-163): the Fermentation Vat at tier 2 with a batch of berry wine at work and its time left, the recipes with what each needs, the next tier's missing parts
The Machinist's Bench (D-163) at tier 2: the Smith's parts, a recipe needing tier 3, an underground recipe, the lathe's parts and skill still missing
The Machinist's Bench in trade premises (seventh pass): two batches of fasteners at work with the seconds left counting down, a finished batch ready to Take, and where a missing part is sold or made
The Pot Still (D-163): licensed grain spirit refused without the Distiller's Licence, moonshine selected as underground work
The pub's counter (D-164): lines the shop buys say what it pays, and the second button sells the bottles the player carries
The Blackwater club's bar (D-201): a short wine line says it buys at the shortage price, with the tooltip explaining why
The work orders page with a Crew contract (D-170): the Crew line counts the parts in, the part orders by career, and the Supplier button for a part nobody can make
Another trade's part of a Crew contract (seventh pass): a Farmer sees the Smith's fittings part, whose it is, where its goods are sold, and the Supplier button
The bonded store job (D-173) accepted and tracked: the order's Track button and the status display pointing at the store
Turning a part to its drawing (D-182): a stretch selected, the tool at a line, roughed sections hatched with tool marks
A section cut below its line shown red, selected, with Sleeve active
A machine's drive stripped at a service call: a worn bearing, a new gear stage, the gear steppers, the plate and the output against it
The Engineer's Toolkit's list of service calls, one out of reach
The glance card at a street door, one of each kind: a pub open until 02:00, a shop and a cased club shut with their opening hour, a public building's hours, a home to let and a house

review_model: CI checks technical screenshot completeness, contrast and duplication; actual artistic/UX judgement requires review of each image after artifact creation.
capture_context: Actual installed client screens, controlled server-snapshot fixtures in main menu. Gameplay transactions separately tested by Forge GameTests.
